title: Improve Dedicated Autoscaler: priority routing, burst smoothing, and utilization reporting
author: Samir Patel
release_notes: Enhances Dedicated autoscaler: adds priority-based routing, token-bucket burst smoothing, priority-aware throughput guarantees, and improved utilization reporting (new metrics + dashboards). No breaking changes to public API.
description:
Motivation: Dedicated fleets have been observed to mis-handle mixed-priority workloads: low-priority traffic can cause head-of-line burst activity that leads to jitter for high-priority routes and inaccurate utilization metrics during burst windows. This PR implements three coordinated improvements: 1) priority-aware routing in the dedicated autoscaler so high-priority routes receive preferential token allocation, 2) a token-bucket smoothing layer for burst controls (configurable EWMA smoothing to avoid abrupt token spikes), and 3) additional utilization reporting metrics and exported Prometheus labels so Console/alerts reflect per-priority utilization and burst consumption.

What changed (high-level):
- Autoscaler core: added PriorityRouter and integrated it with existing token-bucket allocator. New config knobs: priority_weights, min_guarantee_per_priority, burst_smoothing_window_ms.
- Token bucket: refactored token bucket implementation to support EWMA smoothing, time-decoupled refill and consumption accounting to improve stability under noisy clocks.
- Throughput guarantees: added enforcement path that respects per-priority min_guarantees when scaling decisions are made.
- Observability: new metrics (dedicated_autoscaler_tokens_total{priority=..}, dedicated_autoscaler_burst_consumed, dedicated_autoscaler_priority_utilization) + Console dashboard JSON and example alert rules.
- API/Config: extended dedicated fleet config schema (.helm/autoscaler-config.yaml) with new fields and validation. Backwards compatible defaults maintain previous behavior.
- Tests: unit tests for priority routing and token smoothing, integration test exercise mixed-priority workload in perf-canary harness.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc + Linear: ENG-4312 (priority routing) and ENG-4390 (utilization reporting)
- [x] Unit tests added
- [x] Integration canary runs (see perf-canary job)
- [x] Console dashboard and alert cookbook updated
- [x] Docs/upgrade notes added to redwood-docs (link: /docs/dedicated/autoscaler#priority-routing)

Rollout plan:
1) Merge to main behind feature flag enabled_by_default=false.
2) Ship to staging and run canary traffic for 48h (perf-canary).
3) Gradually enable for dedicated fleets in low-risk region, monitor new metrics and alerts.
4) If stable after 7 days, flip default to true and include in next minor release notes.

Notes and risks:
- Defaults preserve existing behavior; enabling exposes additional resource pressure for fleets that rely heavily on bursts. Recommend setting min_guarantee_per_priority on large fleets.
- The EWMA smoothing window may need tuning for very bursty workloads; we added config and a dashboard-driven tuning workflow.

Related: previous burst and reporting PRs (see pr-61234, pr-21437, pr-302601).
